name: Back Extension (45-Degree Hyperextension)
description: The 45-degree back extension is performed on a hyperextension bench and trains hip extension and spinal erector function simultaneously. The lifter flexes forward at the hip and spine under gravity then extends back to neutral or slightly beyond, challenging the erector spinae, gluteus maximus, and hamstrings through a moderate range of motion. This exercise is a primary developer of the posterior chain when performed with controlled technique.

execution.starting_position: Position yourself on the 45-degree hyperextension bench with the front of the thighs resting on the pads. Hook the ankles behind the foot supports. Cross arms over the chest or place hands behind the head. The body should form a straight line in the starting position.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the bench pad height so the hip crease is just above or at the top of the pad — this allows full range of hip flexion. Secure the ankles firmly.
steps: Step 1: Begin in the neutral starting position — body in a straight line from head to hips.
Step 2: Slowly lower the torso toward the floor by hinging at the hips, allowing the spine to flex slightly.
Step 3: Lower until a full stretch is felt in the glutes and hamstrings, or the torso is roughly perpendicular to the floor.
Step 4: Drive the hips into extension and raise the torso back to neutral by contracting the glutes and erectors.
Step 5: At the top, the body should return to a neutral straight line — do not hyperextend the lumbar spine aggressively.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale as you lower the torso. Exhale as you extend back to neutral.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lumbar spine aggressively at the top — stop at neutral or just slightly above
Rounding the upper back excessively at the bottom, which may stress the thoracic spine
Using momentum to swing up rather than controlled muscle contraction
safety_considerations: Avoid excessive spinal hyperextension at the top — this loads the facet joints unnecessarily
If using added weight, hold it at the chest rather than behind the head to reduce cervical strain
Those with existing lower back issues should consult a healthcare professional before performing this exercise
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: From torso perpendicular to the floor at the bottom to neutral body alignment at the top. Some lifters may extend slightly past neutral — avoid aggressive lumbar hyperextension.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the glutes at the top — this cues hip extension rather than lower back arching
Think of your body as a pendulum hinging at the hip
Stop when your body is straight — do not arch further
